item.title: Re: A Plushie Friend
item.content:encoded:
1) How is a Thaumiel-class hazard? It sounds more like a Safe SCP (easy to secure, generally beneficial SCP). You don't want to over-sell it as a problem.

2) Your Hook should be part of the Central Narrative; your hook is simply that it's a stuffed toy that actually protects its owner, which is a cool idea in and of itself.

3) The stuffed animal obviously has limits; it would be nice to see these limits explored. Also, it apparently has some sapience; it would be interesting to see this guy interact with other kid-friendly SCPs, and the link to "Imagination" may give it something in common with SCP-1762 "Here Be Dragons". I know links to other SCPs are frowned on, but in this case they work and enhance the SCP.

Overall, a good concept, but needs some work.

item.title: Re: A train experience based on guilts
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard template, but with an extra "Experiments" section beneath the description

Elevator Pitch: The train is built to replay a situation in which the subject boarding the train has felt most guilty. As such, the person must be capable of thoughts, feelings, and decision-making. The subject, upon entering the train car, will cause its doors to automatically shut and no attempts in opening/prying it open will be successful. After this, the subject will experience a train ride that accelerates constantly until it arrives at a destination. From the outside, no observations of movement or noise can be noted.

The destination in question depends on the situation in which the subject has felt most guilty, whether it be a rejection, a murder, or failure. The experience subjects go through while being 'tested' feels almost dream-like, with unexplainable events or actions occurring. Pain and injuries can still be inflicted in this state. The 'nightmare' will cause subjects to become overwhelmed by guilt, resulting in a high likelihood of suicide or poor decision-making.

Central Narrative: The train station in which the SCP is situated was accidentally stumbled upon by Foundation personnel scouting the area for suspicious missing cases reported by nearby towns. The station did not seem any less normal than any other abandoned station, but an immense sense of guilt and remorse was felt by personnel upon close contact with the train. Strangely enough, residents of nearby towns have reported that this station did not exist according to their knowledge. The Foundation began investigation and experiments on it to determine the possible presence of anomalous properties. Results from these experiments included a bar of metal shaped into a humanoid face resembling fear, decayed organic materials and animals, disappearances of D-classes, and inhumane deaths of D-classes.

One of the unfortunate D-class requested for the experiment was a young caucasian male in his 20s, with a history of murder and arson. Upon the closing of the metallic door, he started to notice that the train had started to move. He struck at the walls of the train with a hammer provided by the Foundation, as instructed before entering the train. The scratching of the wheels across the rails seems to get louder and louder, and the train movement faster and faster. It was almost as if the train was going to de-rail any moment now and he would be riding to his death.

The train suddenly halted, sending the man flying across the train and knocking him unconscious. He awoke to a familiar scenery, one that he had tried to forget about and also the one that brought him to where he is at this moment. The dark ally stood stretching both directions endlessly, and the buildings reaching to the limits of the sky. He recognized the apartment beside him as the one he had set a fire in self-defense against an intruder, which had caused casualties he did not mean to inflict. This is the place where he dies, this is his Hell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Every subject experiences a different kind of 'Hell', and whether they can pass their test purely rests on their own decision-making abilities. No luck, no coincidences, no mishaps, one may find that waking up may never happen. In some cases, their bodies will appear in a museum of some sort, displayed as entertainment and education for extraterrestrial beings. How the train was created is also unknown, perhaps the organization has been studying life on Earth for a while now.

item.title: Re: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
1) The Foundation realizes that there are a lot of civilians that are onto them; this is why they play things off the way they do, using a bit of misdirection and using Weekly World News to deal with SCPs. They expect these guys and are aware of them. However, it's not a bad idea to look at one.

2) The character either needs to be a techno-master or essentially off-line. If he's using a lot of processing power then he needs to be plugged into the grid, but he can't really be bitcoin-miner if he's off-grid. They're two different mindsets so you need to allow for that.

3) Your choice: There are some psuedo-civilian groups out there, so he could join one of those instead of dying. SCP-2137 could save him, or they could just decide that he's got some solid investigative chops, making him a great agent or a great person to have access to. So there are options.

Overall, I like the idea but you need to decide how you're going to approach him right and have some serious fun with him.

item.title: Re: True NPC
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your time and feedback, I see now that I didn't explain some things well enough in the original post (and also, I didn't want to go over the word limit) so I'll try to clarify them here

I divided my response into blocks, each block refers to one "chunk" of your post

+ show block
– hide block

Refrain from calling the SCP an “NPC”. It’s not a programmed character, it’s a sentient or semi-sentient non-physical entity.

I definetly would not call it that in actuall article, I used term NPC here to better explain what it actually is.

+ show block
– hide block

First, the SCP multiverse wasn’t created by the Foundation to stop certain types of anomalies. The multiverse has many different stories about its origin, but the Foundation never had the power to create a whole multiverse.

Afaik there are two kinds of multiverses in Foundation lore. There is the "horizontal" one, the more traditional kind of multiverse, which I think is the one you think about, with many parrarel worlds. I meant the "vertical" kind, the narrative one, where there are many layers of reality, each is like a fiction to the beeings from the "higher" universes. And if "lower" universes are like fiction to us, we can easily create another world, by simply imaging it up.

It is possible I messed up something in the way the fictional layers of reality work, but from what I know it was already reffered in a few SCPs, including the mentioned SCP-3812, SCP-2614 and Database SCP-001 proposal

And here the layers of reality are fictional universes within fictional universes etc. to stop or slow down things that originated somewhere "low" and are somehow resistant to influence from above (because otherwise they would be easily stopped)

And second, I don’t actually think that a self aware RPG character would be able to exist in multiple realities nor have the power to travel between them.

It starts to go up, breaking from the fictional reality to the one higher up. It does not travel between non-fictional parrel universes, nor it exists in more than one. Travelling between fictional worlds if obviously a diffrent thing, since it somehow has to be able to apear in difrent RPGs

Making your SCP overpowered is kinda cliche and a really easy way of getting downvoted.

Yes, I would like to avoid doing another Appolyon or whatever. I understand that its "breaking to the real world" and such seems like its a totally OP thing, but I try my best to 1. make sure it has reasonable limitations 2. there is a way to contain it, that is not overtly complicated and hard to achieve

+ show block
– hide block

Why would his name be a cognitohazard?

Why would its name be a cognitohazard? I thought about hinting on some relationship with fairies, with the power of True Names and such.

Why would its name be clasified by Foundation as a cognitohazard? Because people after seeing it develop a compulsion to include it in their roleplaying games.

Why I, as an author, would I make its name a cognitohazard? It was th central point of the SCP before I came up with the "going up through layers of reality" stuff, it was "a name of an SCP that forces you to roleplay as it during RPGs" and then I played some more with the idea, I read more about pathaphisical SCPs and decided that it makes sense to connect those two things. It is possible that was a bad idea, but without it this SCP lacked some spark for me :v

And if he is a rpg character, how would the Foundation know that he is sentient? If you’re taking about paper and pencil rpg, then it’s basically impossible for a character to be sentient, since the person using that character would choose everything they would do.

That's part of reason why it is anomalous, the person roleplaying as it may seem like its just roleplaying, and it might be indistinguishable most of time, but in some cases (as in some immersion-heavy LARPs) people would do things that will make sense for the character but would not for them to the extreme degree, for example the plot is that the characters are locked in during a blizzard without a food, so the person under the influence of the SCP straight up kills other player, because of fictional reasons. The characters wants and needs "override" the wants and needs of the person roleplaying. That's how the foundation can say that there is something weird going on, and after Foundation's interrogation of this SCP using RPG games they can learn that it is a separate entity from the "host" the person roleplaying as it, and not just a weird effect caused by the SCPs name (altough its a posible reinterpretation, and if this idea will not get greenlighted and will need to be reworked, it might be the path I'll follow).

And yes, I thought about it as a paper and pencil RPG like D&D, rather than computer games like Skyrim and such.

Also, just because a certain character is played multiple times by multiple people doesn’t mean it’s an anomaly, it could mean that a certain character is really famous and people like using him in their roleplaying activities.

That's how it at first evades detection by the Foundation. But in the combination of the cognitohazard caused by its name, people are mentally forced to play as him. Free will and diference with "what if people just want to do that" gets imo tricky when talking about memetic influences.

It's kinda like a diference between, for example, a song that is just very cool and lot of people like it, and a song that forces you to dance to it, even if you wouldn't want to.

+ show block
– hide block

Like I said before, the Foundation isn’t able to build multiple realities, and if they could send entities through these layers, then it would be a infinite loop of the same entity traveling each time to other layers, including our own. The reason why is that, since there are infinite realities, then there is one “below” us with that same entity, and it would eventually reach us again. That’s probably the worst way of containing an SCP, since they would always come back.

I think that I don't fully understand your explanation with the looping realities. I think you may have ment that creation of the copy of Foundation world also copies the entity, but then, given the fact that created universe is moldable like a fiction (except for this SCP and others that are resistant to those changes), a personn creating the copy can just leave out the SCP. It kinda works like elongating the stairs, by adding new steps at the end, and moving previous ones dawnwards, which is not perfect, but allows the Foundation to find other way to stop something that comes to us from fictional realities.

+ show block
– hide block

If you’re going to explore that, you need to describe everything here. That means you need to describe all the effects it causes.

I was limited by the word constraint, and also thought that a greenlight request is supposed to be a qucik summary of what do we wan't to do. I obviously want to include those logs in the article.

I don't know if you want me to write them now, but in case you do, here is some I have thought about, related to the cognitohazardous name (it's obviously a work in progress so it's not all that i think will be there, and what I already thought about might change):

  1. the information is importnat, not the way it's relied. Doesn't matter, if it's read in any alphabet, spoken, or somebody decrypts it in their head, it still will wokr
  2. random string of letters don't work. The name must be created or shown with the awarness that it's a name. If you see for example part of a serial number that is identical to the name of the SCP, it won't work
  3. it only catches on humans so far, monkey that was taught sign language wasn't influenced by it
  4. People exposed to the name, that had no previous contanct with roleplaying create some form of it on their own
+ show block
– hide block

It’s not that interesting to me. I feel this is some kind of bad mix of SCP-3812, SCP-079 and Monika from DDLC. The idea of using other realities is also flawed, since most of it doesn’t make sense. Also, I don’t think an entity that lives inside a roleplaying game could do much, since I believe he would be bound by the laws of that game. So basically, no matter if it’s a paper and pencil rpg or a computer game, it would never be able to leave its realm. I recommend you to remodel the concept and try different things, because I don’t think it would be greenlighted as it is. Good luck! ;)

I understand the connection to SCP-3812 (I made this connection in the orginial post myself) since they work on similar principle of ascesion from fiction to reality, and my idea is a kind of difrent take on it. I kind of see the conection with
SCP-079, with beeing angry about imprisonment (altough I thought it is a kind of common emotion among self aware SCPs contained by Foundation. I would be a bit unhappy myself if I were contained. I didn't play DDLC so can't respond to that.

I understand that it might be not the most interesting, mayby my explanations will make it a bit more appealing. Your feedback made me think about changing some parts of this SCP, eg. going back to original idea, without the ascesion and stuff, and just have a wacky memetic thing that forces poeple to roleplay as certain character, or mayby limit the ascesion, for example that the SCP breaks out to real world, see it's kinda trash, and want's to go back. I would be thankfull for your opinion on those alternatives.

+ show block
– hide block

I would like to thank you again for the time to write the feedback and read my response. I think some of my responses may seem a bit passive-aggresive, it was not my intention, any feedback is very important to me, because then I can correct what I did wrongly and do better next time, so I really apreciate the time you took to look into my idea ^^

item.title: Re: Saint Bernard (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
1) What you have under "Central Narrative" should actually go under "Page Type". The Hook and Elevator Pitch are fine.

2) Kill the Additional Notes; if you're not sure it's a friendly dog and you're the one writing it, then you're wasting people's time. Decide one way or another.

3) SCP-2137 usually only worries about serial killers or other major criminals. If the dog is mentioned by it, then there needs to an actual reason for it, and that should be interesting.

4) The story behind the St. Bernard needs some serious work. Prior history would be nice, such as how long it has been around, some theories as to how it gained its abilities, and even some stories about why it does what it does. We need some details, and there aren't any here.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlights for SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
1) You can convince soldiers that you're one of them in a matter of seconds, especially given the situation (WWII soldiers would have welcomed Resistance help, which was a Dutch thing from 1941). However, if this is a "normal" thing, then it's likely that almost no one would consider it more than a show. However, if you want to interact and have a meaningful conversation, you need more time.

There are the questions of why someone would try to interact with the show and how someone who would want to be close to the guns when they appear would manage that.

2) There needs to be an actual story; there has to be a reason for this particular unit defending against those particular airplanes, and why people are allowed to interact with them. Was the unit losing people, and so sees allowing people to join as a necessity? Could it have been a volunteer battery? You just need some sort of story.

3) So what happens when you interact with the unit besides disappearing with it? And if it's happened before, what does The Foundation know? These are going to help sell your idea, so make sure you include them.

Hello! Thank you for answering!

I worded it poorly. I edited the document and made it so that it specifies that it's a regular SCP, however with more of a narrative structure (think SCP-5000).
I changed it so that the MTF Unit shows development by originally only interacting with the entities for research purposes, however slowly grows to empathize with the fact that they regret their nature. They seem to take a strong interest in the mental functions of these SCPs, leading to an SCP Article with purposefully too much detail - the final draft edited by scientists cuts out much more detail than what is present during it.
I've added a new paragraph detailing the reasoning and secrets behind the entities, which are as follows.

These entities don't wish to create and spectate the chaos which happens, however as if an addiction they depend on it. It is unknown whether they die if there is no chaos spectated. These light creatures are entities born from dying stars, and as such are naturally attracted towards extremely chaotic events, living off of the chaos. Due to the fact that it's one of the few places which are inhabited, these entities seem to enjoy the chaos which comes with this. When times are extremely boring, they seem to create their own manual disasters, usually by moving tectonic plates and creating earthquakes. as they're the easiest to create.

To make the MTF Unit have more development & reasons to care, I gave them a slight amount of backstory explained in this quote.

He empathizes, as he was originally a drug addict who severely struggled to break his addiction. He gains motivation to learn more about them to try and find a way to have the foundation assist in this 'chaos'-addiction, as that's what he always wished he had. This also motivates him to write more so the foundation can understand as much as they can.

It took me a moment to think of a good hook, however I decided on one. It'd be the fact that these creatures seem to have a society, and people they care about, along with emotions and feeling. It gives a side to them other than just 'chaos-lovers'. Diving deeper into the sociability & lives of these creatures which have been created on a foundation of misery & chaos could prove extremely interesting.

I'd rewrite a few thing. Please bear in mind that tone isn't my specialty and these are just suggestions. You may copy them completely or just take elements where you see fit.

I think you containment is direct and effective. I would word it only a bit different but I think they are good.

…database, accessible to personnel with Level 3/XXXX clearance.

I'd stop the first sentence after "database" and then say something like: "Access is granted to…". I'd just split this in two sentences.

All other known copies have been destroyed, and newly discovered copies are to be destroyed as well.

I'd prefer something like: "New copies are destroyed upon discovery as all previously known copies."

As far as the ritual goes I only ask myself some questions with the "anomalously modified strain of the herb". Is this an apart SCP? Is this just a modified plant that grew faster than normal? It might be a nitpick but I think this can easily be solved by adding a small amount of information or re-describing it.

Then on to your main concern: the entity.

In the description you stated that SCP-XXXX-1 is an extradimentional space although I would label the entity which carries the portal (If my interpretation is correct) as SCP-XXXX-1. I would label the other pocket-dimension/Town of Alma (excuse my wording) something else.

I think your description of the entity and its counterpart/behind/… is good. I can visually imagine something close to what you describe. I just think the labeling could be better.

--

As far as the town itself I don't have any remarks. In the shed you have "anomalous heather oil."
I think here its description is not as confusing as the earlier but if you change anything about the plant, check if this is still consistent with the description.

I assume a cot is a bed of linnen or something. English is not my native language. I would leave it as it is but consider "small bed, linnen bed, …" if people get confused by this. If they make no remarks on this, you should probably keep it.

Information suppression was enacted before the offending tweets were reportedly seen by any individuals living outside of the Veil.

Again tone is not my specialty but I think this can be described differently. Suppression and offending don't seem completely out of place but changing a bit here can make it more clinical in my opinion.

…were reportedly seen by any individuals living outside of the Veil.

I'd change "reportedly seen" to "seen" or "witnessed". I don't know about mentioning the Veil. Perhaps "were leaked to the public." is an option to consider.

Small nitpick: the tweet itself is ok but you have a typo (are instead of our). If you can't fix this I can assume that it is an autocorrect.

I don't know if Class-A amnestics are enough but that is your choice. I personally go with Class-B most of the time. I know she kind of remembers since she almost literally spells it out in the addendum, but the Foundation probably won't take chances with taking amnestics like this. Perhaps you can mention she is somewhat resistant to amnestic since she comes from a branch in the Chaos Insurgency or just include a bit of thaumaturgy.

The addendum serves as an explanation and I think the format you used is fine. I don't 100% know how to crit a sms-conversation though. I'd expect texts to be shorter and have less
punctuation marks etc. but again they have that background of the insurgency so that it isn't too "loosely". I advise you to seek someone good with dialogue if you want to check tone on this. It is a good addition but doesn't completely hit for me/feels a bit off.

Overall I'd say whilst your draft is interesting and has some good content, you need to work on some loose ends and polish it here and there.

If you have to wait a lot for additional crit I advise you to go to the chat/IRC, I think you will find what you need there.

Good luck

Some concepts, such as "SCP-682" and "Transcendence", are currently outside and cannot become inside.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

The anomalies are not naturally drawn to each other. They can exist in entirely opposing sections of the world and may continue along with their anomalous existence completely unaware of the existence of the other and feel no urge to be brought together.
Anomalies that don't possess physical bodies and a semblance of sapience don't have counterparts. To clarify, an anomaly must be a living being in order to have a counterpart, and thus places or events do not possess one where people and animals do.

What brings them together is an anomalous annual event wherein the two foundations "meet" each other and come increasingly closer to merging at the will of SCP staff, who become more and more difficult to stop or dissuade with each occurrence. If they weren't separated in two, it would be much easier for the staff to end up bringing these two anomalies together; A mismanagement during transfers would be fairly detrimental.

What I'm trying to get at is that when some of the more powerful anomalies come together, especially ones with a distaste for life, it would invariably lead to a K-Class scenario. I intend to focus on SK, where the anomalies either take over the planet or destroy humanity, but of course there are others with other intents and some without intents that would ruin reality regardless. What I want to try to do is allow the reader some room to fill in the blanks and come up with their own counterparts or scenarios. What would 507's hightened anomalous powers be if he came into contact with his entirely-immobile counterpart? Instead of him shifting into other realities, does he bring those realities to us?

I guess I just feel as though if I answered every little thing about what could happen, it might kill some of the magic for the reader. I'm trying to figure out how to leave things just open-ended enough to leave the reader with a solid understanding of how things work but also with a dread of the possible counterparts, and powers granted to the possible couples.

Edit: I should mention that I am most certainly going to mention the potential for complete restructuring, shuffling, or destruction of reality, but I don't intend to make it a major focus, just a lingering potential threat.

item.title: Re: The Friendly Shadow
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I….don't really like this. I like what you're trying to do; but the actual execution feels all over the place: there's so much jumping around topics and themes that the core narrative feels muddier than it should.

Decisions like not introducing -2 until the midpoint, instead of mentioning it explicitly in both the Description and the Discovery contribute to this: it has a feeling of introducing new elements to force character growth to occur; whereas if all the pieces had been laid out at the start, you could just, have the characters react: the whole thing around -1 being the passenger for the shadow can come up naturally when the interviewer asks about the painting, instead of in this weird forced way.

The disappearance of Agent Wolf is a like, technically interesting plot thread that never feels like it goes anywhere: Wolf is brought up immediately as they disappear so we don't really get invested in bringing them back, but other than a token question to Thomas in the one interview, it's never really explored in any way and it really feels like it could be cut: the painting doesn't need to be made explicitly anomalous, it could be made interesting and asked about purely from the discovery log noting SCP-XXXX was watching it.

I think though the core issue from the storytelling is that all the interesting stuff is in the relation between Thomas and Clarence, but there's barely any times where they actually interact in a tangible way: the discovery and the short video log being the only real times; the first interview kinda does but in a disconnected way where the shadow is definitely interacting with Clarence but not in a way that we, the reader, can grok and so it doesn't really add to their relationship. And so the arc feels rushed: there's never really a chance for this to establish what their relationship is like for the reader as a baseline really, or for us to get a feel for their characters; and so when this relationship is shifted up by Thomas confessing to Clarence, we don't really have a way to predict what this will do. The other problem is that the entire 'revelation, fallout, attempt to reconcile' thing takes place in 500 words: it never really gets the time it needs to show how this affects either of the characters or for them to tangibly grow as a result of this; and so it feels…lacking.

I can definitely see this being rewritten to work better but…it feels to me like it'd need a really thorough editing pass where you really consider how the story flows a lot more and then really figure out how you can best convey the flow.

In it's current state, this would be a -1 from me, and I would guess most other readers would feel the same way.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

Following incident XXXX-A2, SCP-XXXX-1 has been provided with counseling and further education within Site-17.

I'd probably move the 'within Site-17' earlier into the ConProcs; perhaps right after noting it's kept in a humanoid containment chamber.

SCP-XXXX is the shadow of SCP-XXXX-1, a humanoid appearing as a 36-year-old male of Caucasian descent.

Caucasian descent means 'descended from someone from the Caucasus region'; I think you want e.g. 'white American male' here say instead.

I'm also a little iffy about introducing two SCP designations in the first 6 words of your SCP: it feels like perhaps introducing the shadow first and then later the human it's attached to would read better but?

SCP-XXXX-1 identifies as Clarence Carter.

'identifies' here implies 'this is a fake name'; I'd use 'is known as' say

SCP-XXXX has the illuminated outline of a mouth, eyes, and body similar to that of SCP-XXXX-1.

'similar to that' here implies -1 has an illuminated outline of these features too, I'd suggest a semi-colon before similar and perhaps 'similar in appearance' say?

SCP-XXXX is able to detach itself from SCP-XXXX-1 to interact with shadows of objects or people.

I feel like 'interact with other shadows' would be clearer here; and wouldn't have the weird implication that it can't interact with e.g. animals and plants

For more information, see Addenda.

I'd cut this; if you're not specifying a specific place that covers this, it's not necessary. Even if you are, it feels…odd? Like just trust a reader to assume you'll show this, y'know?

SCP-XXXX was discovered on December 3rd, 20██

Why does knowing the exact date this was discovered on pose a security risk? IMO: unredact this date, and later dates, so we have a concrete idea of the timeline that this is taking place over; as opposed to the current possibility of the discovery being up to 98 years before the rest.

Following SCP-XXXX-1's arrest at the Virginia State Museum, it was observed that SCP-XXXX-1 did not have a shadow.

I feel like it'd be a good idea to hint at why -1 was arrested here; y'know, use the crime to characterise what they're like.

Embedded Foundation agents reported the anomaly and removed it, amnesticised witnesses.

'the anomaly' is singular which implies they only removed one of SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1; and I'd be clear about which it is here.

The 'amnesticised witnesses' is too 'fragmentary'; it really needs a few more words e.g. 'before they amnesticised witnesses' say.

SCP-XXXX was contained by MTF Iota-10 ("Damn Feds"). The two objects were collectively designated as SCP-XXXX.

Not really a fan of the vague 'oh yeah a MTF just, contained the shadow' here; and also the two objects were not collectively designated as SCP-XXXX.

It should be noted that SCP-XXXX is referred as "Thomas" by SCP-XXXX-1.

<SCP-XXXX observes SCP-XXXX-2

-2 is defined ~750 words after this. This doesn't flow right as a result because we have no idea what's happening. Even just using 'observes a painting' with a 'later designated SCP-XXXX-2' footnote would be better.

you're also missing the closing > here

Possible that he’s holding back on details.

I'd add an 'It's' at the start here; this feels weirdly note like

He made a sudden change of opinion on the topic of whether to be separated from SCP-XXXX in further interviews when SCP-XXXX made an abrupt change of pace.

This is written here like it's summarising something that happened within the interview but it's not so it feels really weird? Like if it was summarising something, it'd be unnecessary cos we'd read it; but instead it appears to be info that Rose has just plucked out of the air.

LEVEL 3 CLEARANCE REQUIRED - INPUT CREDENTIALS

This feels altogether too short a note to be in a collapsible.

Agent Hart found Agent Wolf had disappeared while examining a painting on exhibit.

'on exhibit' feels weird to me; maybe 'in the exhibition' or 'on display' would be clearer?

Something about this construction is weird; it kinda implies Hart walked in, saw Wolf had disappeared and then just like, pointed at a random painting and said 'this did it'. It'd work better if there was more of a concrete link between this painting and the one referred to earlier but it feels like Hart should actually like…see this happening?

Efforts to retrieve Agent Wolf are in progress.

'underway' would be better than 'in progress' here.

After the retrieval of the anomalous painting

you've given it a designation by now, use the designation.

// <XXXX interacts

the space between // and < has broken your italics here.

//How about this. I'll answer anything you need to know, and you answer a few of my questions in return.

missing the closing // here

idea. And the thought of that alone terrifies me.
// <XXXX

space issue again; also missing an empty line between these

"Look, giving you answers will only lead to more questions. Questions you wish to have answers to. Some questions shouldn't be answered, Doctor."

you've got a big chunk of this interview repeating here a few times; it's very weird and I think accidental?

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
+ Responses
- Close

To start with, considering the individuals in the center of the earth wouldn’t be able to see anything, how would they (and subsequently the Foundation) know where they were? I’m rather sure geolocation is harder when you’re literally at the center of the earth; however, that’s something else that could be hand-waved away as ‘co-opted anomalous tech’.

The individuals don't know they are at the center of the earth. The Foundation knows by tracing communication from the anomalous tech.

If the Foundation isn’t pursuing a way to get people back from the core of the earth, then what exactly are the people on the surface doing while they’re receiving these messages?

Researching and monitoring the anomaly. Attempting two-way communication with the person (which they have been pursuing). Other stuff not related to this anomaly. Recovering the people isn't the Foundations goal, containing and understanding the anomaly is.

I’m also going to ask what may sound like a bit of a weird question: why the center of the earth? It seems like any inhospitable plane of existence could be substituted in with minimal change to the plot. This tends to be a bad sign, in my experience.

The center of the earth idea was originally from another idea, which this is a revision of, however, I do have reason for currently using the center of the earth. Plains, near-death states and other similar experiences are usually the result of a central cause. A doorway, an entity, an experiment gone wrong. This anomaly isn't like any of those.

This anomaly is an inevitability in a world with intangibility. This anomaly isn't due to a central cause or because of a central reason, it's a conglomeration of causes and reasons built up over centuries. Even if the Foundation rescued all the people from the core, that wouldn't neutralize the anomaly, as it would soon start growing again. As long as humanity exists, we will seek power. Along as intangibility exists, we will used it to gain power. And as long as this continues to happen, this anomaly will persist. That is the true horror of the article, not just the story of the one person, the fact that that experience will continue to happen to people indefinitely, and there's no good or simple way to stop it. This separates the center of the earth experience from similar experiences and there are very few other concepts I feel could bring the same horror.

Some small nitpicks, less important than the overall thoughts below:

The sand also appears to have some degree of sapience/conscious and can react if communicated with or attacked.

I think the idea of this anomaly being aggressive with people isn't necessary for it to be interesting… it could have been discovered because someone went on the beach and shit started forming out of the sand around them in response to their thoughts… I find the idea that it was ever aggressive a little underutilized here.

During tests and communications with the SCP, it's implied that other beings we're involved in the War between the True and False. The SCP mentions they were lead into the battle by a woman 'surrounded in moonlight' and that she was lost during the endgame of the war, along with her 'grand family'.

Although I appreciate what you're trying to do here, you have a grand story you wanna tell… keep in mind this first article needs to survive on its own thing. So keep whatever hinting at grander lore incredibly vague, and don't make it be the central revelation. You never know what may happen, maybe the article doesn't survive… maybe you don't end up wanting to tell the story you have in mind. For those reasons keep any lore hints vague and openended so later you could take it up if you wanted.

Overall: So I am a sucker for Greek Myth, and this isn't something grandiose like Zeus or Hades or whatever, so I dig that. But my concern is that here is a premise for a story that revolves entirely around these creatures being something of myth.

There's no twist, nothing to do the unexpected… and there doesn't seem to be much of a personal connection. You mention we're supposed to feel sad for them, but if you want that, you have to make them relatable to your reader.

Additionally, if they are mountain nymphs… why are they on the beach and made of sand? I believe there are sea nymphs, so why not make them those? I just think there's a disconnect between the resulting anomaly and its origins.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
So, on the one hand I see you reaching for a more satisfying ending… I don't think either of these two option as presented would work.

  • If you want to go for the haunting/sad thing, I wouldn't suggest suicide but instead the representation of something anomalous coming to grips with his future as a contained anomaly by the foundation… Yeah this is harder, but would be more satisfying
  • If you want to go for the whole "I have the purpose I decide" (which has narrative chops) I would want to know more about this current purpose… as I understand the anomaly, he doesn't seem like he would be much help with anything. His anomaly is that he was a fictional character which was made manifest. So how could he help the foundation such that they would buy in (along with the reader).
    • an alternative would be what is anyone's purpose? Its not such an easy answer, and it could be something as simple as existing and getting free… or trying to find what happiness he can while in containment.
    • Either way, I think what you're missing is the human connection… I would suggest fostering a relationship with either a researcher or counselor assigned to his case. Then he could explore his meaning in the world through that connection, and would add emotional stakes.

Either way, I think you have the makings of the decent article and think the rest could be ironed out in the drafting. So have a GREENLIGHT

Thanks for being a psychic and posting this on a day where the world, or at least my country, needed a touch of brightness. +1

item.title: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
Hello there!
Interesting SCP you've got here…
Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So, I'm going to be honest, I love this idea. I really, really like the story, the characters, the anomaly, all that good stuff, it's perfect. So I'm going to go ahead and give you a greenlight.
However, I do have some of concerns I'd like you to take care of before going through with your idea. This is the same concern that Cybersqyd pointed out. The story is predictable, primarily because we know about the affects of the anomaly. So, the way that I'm going to suggest that you overcome this is by leaving the actual description towards the end. Maybe have the person writing the article be affected by the waves? They keep writing the wrong things? Or going off topic? Perhaps there can be 4-5 different descriptions between the addendums, and at the very end of your paper is an actual description of the anomalous properties, with an ominous ending indicating that the SCP has reeked some sort of unknown havoc onto the foundation.
Please do reach out if you have any questions about the story line/article! And keep me posted on how the article turns out. You can reach me by pm if you need help. Best of luck with the article!

item.title: Re: New author need greenlight for idea
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PMs
Sorry for the late reply
Here lies the crit:

+ show block
– hide block

Overall, while I do think this concept has potential, it's falling really flat in terms of the story. There's no narrative, no event, no character that your article revolves around. You need something more than just "This SCP did this thing and this thing and this thing". It needs to be much more detailed. For example, what may have happened if the SCP did come into contact with another SCP at one point? Maybe have a video transcript of the containment breach? Or maybe have an interview with someone who discovered it/provide some solid backstory for it? Maybe provide a log of contact with aliens? Something like that. Just spice up the story. You have a solid Foundation, but you need to build up on it from there. Unfortunately, until you create an acceptable story, I won't be able to Greenlight it. But if you would like me to take a second look, please do reach out!
